description: GEPPAA is an Astronomy and Astrophysics group at UNILAB, Brazil, dedicated to teaching, research, and science outreach. We promote astronomy through educational activities, telescope observations, and scientific projects. Our interests include astrophysics, mathematics, image processing, and space exploration. We welcome collaborators skilled in programming, data science, and technology to develop creative solutions together.
summary:
URUTAU is an interactive astronomy platform that uses data from NASA’s SPHEREx space telescope to explore the sky across different observation periods. Users can select sky regions through coordinates or an interactive map, access available observations, and visualize sequences of astronomical images as time-based animations.

The platform aims to help users identify objects that move or vary over time through image comparison, astrometric visualization, and astronomical source analysis tools. It transforms large scientific datasets into an accessible and engaging exploration experience.

URUTAU brings the public closer to real space mission data, encourages citizen science, and demonstrates how technology, mathematics, and astronomy can work together to explore the universe.
details:
URUTAU: The Sky in Motion is an astronomical exploration platform designed to make data from NASA's SPHEREx space telescope accessible to everyone, regardless of their technical background.

Our main goal is to enable students, educators, astronomy enthusiasts, and researchers to explore the sky visually and intuitively, without needing prior knowledge of celestial coordinates. Through an interactive sky map, users can navigate the sky, select a region, or search for an astronomical object by name or coordinates.

The platform uses astronomical archive services, particularly NASA/IPAC IRSA, to query SPHEREx observations. Available records can be organized by observation date, detector, and wavelength. After selecting images, users can explore them as a time-based sequence, control frame-by-frame playback, adjust brightness and contrast, zoom into regions, and compare observations. The application also includes astrometric analysis tools, customizable object annotations, and a local investigation notebook for saving information and exporting reports.

URUTAU's creativity lies in combining accessibility, temporal visualization, and scientific tools within a single experience. Instead of requiring users to understand complex astronomical archive interfaces, the platform provides a simple workflow: explore the sky, select images, observe changes, and document discoveries.

The project was developed using TypeScript, React, Vite, Node.js, Express, Electron, Aladin Lite, and astronomical image-processing libraries, alongside integrations with services such as NASA/IPAC IRSA, Gaia, and SIMBAD. Generative artificial intelligence tools, including Google Gemini and OpenAI ChatGPT, assisted with code implementation, user interface organization, documentation, and testing. The project's concepts, objectives, and requirements were defined by the project team.

No specialized astronomical equipment is required to use URUTAU. Users only need a computer and an internet connection to access scientific data.

Our intended impact is to expand public access to astronomy, encourage citizen science, and provide an educational tool for investigating apparent motion and brightness variations in celestial objects using observations from space missions.

The project also emphasizes data traceability, source attribution, observation quality, and scientific limitations. Its scientific features are undergoing validation with real astronomical data, and user annotations are not automatically considered confirmed discoveries.
